segments.title: Chương 178: Nữ Sinh Manga Bị Tẩy Chay Hội Đồng
segments.content:
Chapter 181 0178: Manga Girl Suffers Social Death

Xu Fengyin's photos going viral was purely an accident.

Chen Guiliang had arranged for professional photographers to take pictures of his cosplayers. Every shot was exquisitely captured and posted on major forums and Tieba.

These photos did generate some buzz, but they were far from causing a sensation.

The ones that truly went viral were, coincidentally, a set of amateur photos.

Taken with a 3.0-megapixel digital camera, the angle, focus, and lighting were far from professional, purely the work of an ordinary convention attendee.

But they blew up!

The photos were first posted on the ICV Forum, a community under an anime news website.

The post's title was also unremarkable, showing no potential for going viral. It was called: A Pretty Cosplayer Off Duty.

The first photo showed Xu Fengyin standing below the side of the stage, looking at her phone after the cosplay competition had ended. Her face was flushed red from the heat, a sweat-dampened strand of hair stuck to her cheek.

The second photo showed Xu Fengyin squatting by the roadside, raising her left hand to tuck her hair behind her ear while her right hand was pressing her phone's keypad, replying to a text.

The third photo showed Xu Fengyin noticing she was being photographed and waving at the camera with a smile. There was a hint of awkwardness in her smile, probably because she felt her squatting posture was ungraceful.

The fourth photo showed Xu Fengyin back at the Sanguosha booth, standing there drowsily yawning.

The fifth photo showed Xu Fengyin realizing she was being followed and photographed, frowning and glaring at the photographer to express her displeasure.

"Wow, this cosplayer is so pretty."

"Keep it up, OP! This set of photos is very natural. I saw the other official photos, and while they're beautifully shot, they're all too posed and artificial."

"What game character is this?"

"Zhen Ji from Sanguosha."

"I especially love the last one, frowning and glaring at someone. She looks so pretty when she's mad."

"The second one is the best, tucking her hair back while playing with her phone. Her side profile from that angle is gorgeous."

"Haha, this is my little junior from the Academy of Fine Arts. She used to draw illustrations for *Man You*, and now she's working as an artist at Youke. She was probably grabbed by her company to be a cosplayer at the last minute."

"So she's a manga artist, so talented!"

"Senior, what's your little junior's QQ number?"

"What the! She's Jiuneng Daidao? I've even seen her risqué manga."

Accidentally, Xu Fengyin's dark history was unearthed. The netizens of ICV followed the trail and found several manga she had posted before.

It wasn't really anything much, just girls being intimate with each other, with nothing inappropriate exposed.

The most exquisitely drawn one was of Akane Tendo and Shampoo getting close, a pairing that could only be described as bizarre.

Soon, some netizens from the ICV forum reposted Xu Fengyin's photos and risqué works to the Cosplay Bar and Manga Bar.

A pure and beautiful female artist, and risqué, alluring manga—this magical combination instantly set the two Tieba ablaze.

Then, it was reposted to the Ranma Bar, Sailor Moon Bar, and a bunch of other manga-related Tieba. Only after that was it reposted to Tianya Forum, Xici Hutong, Mop...

"Ah!!!"

Xu Fengyin sat in front of her computer, holding her head and letting out a low, miserable cry.

She felt like she had suffered a social death.

She had always been afraid of people in her real life discovering that she created risqué manga.

And now, those manga had been dug up and were going viral across the internet along with photos of her.

Xu Fengyin could imagine the scene. She'd go downstairs to eat, and people would point at her and whisper: Look, that's the one who draws risqué manga online...

Also, what if her parents saw it?

Xu Fengyin logged into her ICV account, deleted all her posts, then deactivated her account to destroy the evidence.

If her parents, relatives, or friends asked, she would deny it to the death, saying that netizens were spreading rumors and slandering her!

Next, Xu Fengyin logged into her Kaixin001 account. Some netizens had already followed the trail there. This was because during the exhibition, she had taken the time to post a set of her own cosplay photos.

Beneath those photos, there were dense rows of comments, among which were plenty of anime nerds who had come to declare their love.

Some believed it, some didn't.

Xu Fengyin kept refreshing the comments, her heart pounding with guilt as she read the replies.

"How could such a pure MM draw that kind of stuff? You people are so disgusting!"

"It's not disgusting. I think it's drawn quite beautifully, and there's no inappropriate exposure."

"You can't hide an art style. With my years of experience as a manga fan, Jiuneng Daidao is definitely this girl's alternate account."

A Youke programmer, returning from the restroom, passed by Xu Fengyin's desk, gave her a thumbs-up, and said, "Great God Xu, keep it up! Looking forward to your new work."

Xu Fengyin flatly denied it: "I didn't draw that!"

"I believe you." The programmer colleague winked at her.

Xu Fengyin covered her face in despair.

What should I do?

I have no face to show anyone.

Xu Fengyin typed out a resignation letter on her keyboard, but when she got to the reason for resignation, she didn't know what to make up.

Besides, she was in charge of the art for Sanguosha, and the company had even hired two assistants for her, asking her to take on apprentices and train the newcomers. If she just resigned and left, it would be too irresponsible.

Xu Fengyin pretended to go to the restroom, took the elevator upstairs, and went straight to Bytedance.

A few employees looked over. Xu Fengyin, with her "guilty conscience," felt that there was something off about their gazes.

"Secretary Hu, I'm looking for President Chen."

"Just knock on the door yourself."

After moving, Chen Guiliang finally had his own private office, with an outer room partitioned off for his secretary, Hu Yuexia, during the renovation.

There were only about a hundred people now, so there weren't too many rules.

Any employee with a special situation could go directly to Chen Guiliang.

Even that system of job ranks was somewhat redundant; there was no need to make things so complicated for a company with fewer than 150 people. It was just to set the rules in advance, preparing for future expansion.

"Knock, knock, knock."

"Come in."

Chen Guiliang had been away from the company for over half a month. A pile of matters that weren't extremely urgent but still required his personal attention had accumulated and needed to be dealt with quickly.

"Is it about the photos going viral?" Chen Guiliang already knew.

Game Science's marketing and planning staff were currently riding the wave, using this surge in popularity to promote Sanguosha.

"Mhm."

Xu Fengyin nodded.

The reason she had come to see Chen Guiliang was because he knew her bigger secret, which made the risqué manga affair seem trivial in comparison.

Besides, she felt that President Chen would definitely have a solution.

"Boss, what should I do? I'm too embarrassed to face anyone," Xu Fengyin asked.

Chen Guiliang said, "Don't take any unnecessary actions. The more you try to explain, the more suspicious netizens will become. Just act like nothing happened, and this will blow over soon enough."

"Huh? But I just posted on Kaixin001 saying Jiuneng Daidao isn't my alternate account," Xu Fengyin asked, "Does that count as an unnecessary action?"

Chen Guiliang said with an amused smile, "It does, but it's not a big deal. Don't delete that post either."

Xu Fengyin said weakly, "I deleted all my old posts on ICV..."

"Then there's no explaining it. You've only made it more conspicuous," Chen Guiliang tapped his forehead with a finger. "Next time, use your brain more before you act. If Jiuneng Daidao wasn't your alternate account, why would Jiuneng Daidao delete the posts?"

Xu Fengyin slapped her forehead in regret. "I was in such a panic, I wasn't thinking straight."

Chen Guiliang said, "Go draw. When you start drawing, you'll forget everything else."

"Then how do I interact with my colleagues? I always feel like they're looking at me funny," Xu Fengyin asked for advice.

Chen Guiliang said, "Interact with them the same way you always have. The more you show you care, the more they'll overthink it. If someone teases you or makes a few jokes about it, I think that's within an acceptable range. If someone's words are really out of line, just tell me directly. If it's confirmed, I'll privately warn them. If they still don't listen, I'll fire them."

"Thank you, Boss." Xu Fengyin felt this was feasible.

"Go on."

"Goodbye, Boss."

Xu Fengyin walked out, forcing herself to act calm. She had to pretend nothing had happened.

Secretary Hu Yuexia knocked and came in again. "President Chen, Manyou Culture wants to schedule a meeting to discuss the physical card game distribution rights for the mainland."

Hu Yuexia was nominally an employee of Bytedance, but for news that Game Science needed to report, they would sometimes call her for help with scheduling.

Chen Guiliang said, "Let Youke's business development specialist handle it."

Manyou Culture was the parent company of *Man You* magazine, and they were in talks to distribute *Yu-Gi-Oh!*. But the asking price for *Yu-Gi-Oh!* was too high, with a licensing fee of over one million yuan, an outrageous 35% revenue share, and an extremely high minimum guarantee.

Manyou Culture turned its attention to *Sanguosha*. They had made initial contact at the Shanghai convention, but after two rounds of talks, they failed to reach an agreement.

The licensing fee and revenue share were actually negotiable, but Manyou Culture had another demand: for Youke to terminate its cooperation with online bookstores and Taobao shops. Even Youke's own Taobao store had to be transferred to Manyou Culture!

Chen Guiliang had planned to leave them hanging for a few days. Unexpectedly, just after he returned to Beijing, Manyou Culture contacted him again.

They were probably in a hurry, afraid another company would snatch the deal.

This was because they had discovered that the news about the Korean player calling Chinese people idiots and Chen Guiliang demanding an apology was still gaining traction even after the convention ended. Many print and online media outlets were discussing the phenomenon of Korean online games flooding the Chinese market.

At the same time, Youke was promoting *Sanguosha*'s successful overseas expansion, having already sold rights to South Korea, Hong Kong, and Taiwan.

Coupled with Xu Fengyin's Zhen Ji cosplay photos gaining traction...

*Sanguosha*'s popularity was steadily rising, and it was highly likely that another company interested in distributing the card game would emerge.

Manyou Culture's concerns were well-founded. On the third day of Chen Guiliang's return to Beijing, "Waiyanshe" proactively sought them out for a partnership.

"Waiyanshe" was the full name for the Foreign Language Teaching and Research Press, and its name told you what it did.

They believed *Sanguosha* was an educational card game that could also spread historical knowledge. They would directly play the education card—Three Kingdoms Historical Knowledge Cards—and leverage their monopolistic advantage in Xinhua Bookstores and school channels to sell *Sanguosha* cards!

In the end, Chen Guiliang chose to partner with Waiyanshe.

Even though Waiyanshe's offer was far lower than Manyou Culture's.

But Waiyanshe offered a condition that was hard to refuse: they would use all their power to crack down on piracy.

(End of Chapter)
